issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Farm: the problem statement explicitly requires a no-argument constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList of animals ("Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments") and the template Main example instantiates Farm with new Farm(), but the solution repository provides only a parameterized constructor public Farm(int initialCapacity) (no no-arg constructor). This prevents code that follows the problem text or the provided Main example (new Farm()) from compiling against the solution implementation and will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem statement and template by adding a no-argument constructor that initializes the animals list, for example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } (you may also keep the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor as an overload). Alternatively, if the parameterized constructor was intentional, update the problem statement and the example Main.java to show and use the parameterized form (e.g., new Farm(10)).
